speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To better understand your condition, could you tell me if these symptoms started suddenly or developed gradually over time? Also, do you notice any drooping of your eyelids or difficulty swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the fluctuation with activity is a significant clue. Are you experiencing any fatigue during the day, and do you have a history of thyroid disease or myasthenia gravis? Also, do you experience any difficulty speaking or chewing?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies, Anti-MuSK_Antibodies. REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Chest. Do you have any known endocrine disorders, and how severe is your difficulty climbing stairs compared to your baseline?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated); Anti-MuSK_Antibodies: Not detected; CT_Chest: Normal, no thymoma or other masses detected. No known endocrine disorders reported. Difficulty climbing stairs: Unable to assess severity compared to baseline; patient reports symmetrical weakness in arms and legs that worsens with activity and improves with rest, but specific stair-climbing metrics were not provided in the current data.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The elevated Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies, combined with your symptoms of fluctuating weakness that worsens with activity and improves with rest, along with ocular involvement, confirm this diagnosis. The normal CT chest rules out a thymoma, suggesting the non-thymomatous form of the disease.
